title: Low System Pressure
shortDescription: Hydronic loop pressure has fallen below the minimum threshold.
fullDescription:
Buderus Logamatic GB142 and SSB units display 2P when the integrated pressure transducer reads below ~7 psi (0.5 bar). The boiler will not fire to protect the heat exchanger.

Low pressure on a sealed system points to either a leak, a waterlogged expansion tank, or normal early-life venting of dissolved gases. Refill via the manual fill valve to 12-15 psi cold and observe.
safetyWarning: Do not over-pressurize; the relief valve will discharge above 30 psi.

causes.cause: Slow leak in piping or radiator vent

fixSteps.title: Refill to spec
fixSteps.instruction: Open the fill valve until the gauge reads 12-15 psi (0.8-1 bar) cold.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check radiator vents, circulator flanges, relief valve discharge.

fixSteps.title: Test expansion tank
fixSteps.instruction: Tap the tank; a hollow sound is good, dull/heavy is waterlogged.

whenToCallPro: If pressure drops repeatedly within days — there is a leak that needs locating.

faq.q: How often should I add water?
faq.a: Almost never on a sealed system — repeated refills mean a leak.

title: High System Pressure
shortDescription: Loop pressure is above the maximum allowed.
fullDescription: 3P appears when the pressure transducer reads above ~30 psi (2.5 bar). Most often this is a failed pressure-reducing/auto-fill valve that is letting house water continuously feed the loop, or a waterlogged expansion tank that cannot accept thermal expansion.
safetyWarning: Excessive pressure will trigger relief-valve discharge — keep clear of hot water.

fixSteps.title: Isolate auto-fill
fixSteps.instruction: Close the cold-feed valve to the boiler temporarily.

fixSteps.title: Bleed to 1 bar
fixSteps.instruction: Open a low-point drain to reduce pressure to 12-15 psi.

fixSteps.title: Tank check
fixSteps.instruction: Verify expansion-tank air precharge with a gauge while system is depressurized.

whenToCallPro: If the auto-fill or expansion tank needs replacement.

faq.q: Why does pressure climb only when hot?
faq.a: Classic waterlogged expansion tank symptom.

title: Supply Sensor Open
shortDescription: Boiler outlet temperature sensor is open-circuit.
fullDescription:
4Y means the supply (heat-exchanger outlet) NTC reads open. The control disables firing because it cannot enforce limit protection.

Most often a connector worked loose during service or the sensor cable was pinched when the cover was reinstalled.
safetyWarning: Power off before disconnecting sensor leads.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the supply sensor harness at the BC10/BC25.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm at room temp; should be near 12kΩ on Buderus NTC. Replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Sensor well replacement requires draining the boiler.

faq.a: Use the OEM Buderus part to match the temperature curve.

title: Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Burner failed to establish flame after ignition retries.
fullDescription: 6A is the Buderus ignition lockout. After three failed ignition attempts the GB142/SSB locks out and waits for manual reset. Causes mirror other condensing boilers: low gas, fouled electrode, blocked condensate, or a failed gas valve.
safetyWarning: If you smell gas evacuate and call your gas emergency line.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm gas is on at the boiler valve.

fixSteps.title: Clean electrode
fixSteps.instruction: If recurring, clean and gap the ignition assembly.

whenToCallPro: Gas valve or pressure work requires a licensed gas tech.

faq.a: Two; if it returns the third time, stop.

title: Flame Lost During Run
shortDescription: Established flame disappeared during a heat call.
fullDescription: 6C is logged when the unit ignites successfully but loses flame during the burn. Common reasons are a failing flame rod losing rectification, momentary low gas pressure, or condensate blocking the flue.
safetyWarning: Repeated mid-run flame loss can produce unburned gas — investigate before resetting again.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame rod
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, pull and lightly polish the flame rod.

fixSteps.title: Inspect flue
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the vent looking for sags pooling condensate.

whenToCallPro: Gas-pressure verification or vent rework.

faq.a: No — 6C is purely a flame-supervision event.

title: Gas Valve Drive Fault
fullDescription: 6L is a safety lockout from the control's gas-valve supervision circuit. Possible causes are a shorted gas valve coil, a damaged harness, or a failed control board.
safetyWarning: Treat as a serious gas-valve fault and isolate gas.

fixSteps.title: Isolate gas
fixSteps.instruction: Close the manual gas valve on the boiler inlet.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a tech ohm the gas valve coil and inspect the board.

whenToCallPro: Always — this is gas-valve supervision lockout.

faq.q: Can a power surge cause this?
faq.a: Yes; surges damage the FETs that drive the gas valve coil.

title: Pressure Switch / APS Open
shortDescription: Air pressure switch did not close after fan start.
fullDescription: 9B indicates the inducer ran up to speed but the air-proving switch never closed. Either the fan is not actually moving air or the switch/hose is faulty.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass — this protects against vent obstruction and CO spillage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Clear any blockage; verify in winter for ice/snow.

fixSteps.title: Test hose
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the pressure-switch hose for cracks or condensate.

whenToCallPro: Blower or pressure switch replacement.

faq.a: Not directly — the switch prevented operation. Always have a working CO alarm.

title: High Limit Trip
fullDescription: 9H means the manual or auto high limit opened. Hydronic causes: air-bound HX, dead pump, closed isolation valve. The control will lock out until reset.
safetyWarning: Investigate the flow problem before resetting.

fixSteps.title: Bleed
fixSteps.instruction: Vent the boiler and high points of the loop.

fixSteps.title: Verify flow
fixSteps.instruction: Touch supply piping during a call — should warm quickly with circulator on.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement or persistent recurrence.

faq.q: Why right after a power outage?
faq.a: Air enters the system; bleed thoroughly.

title: Fan Feedback Out of Range
shortDescription: Combustion blower RPM does not match command.
fullDescription: A1 is reported when the fan tach signal and the PWM command disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Worn brushes, debris fouling, or a bad PWM cable are usual.
safetyWarning: Disconnect line voltage at the cabinet before fan work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove inlet, vacuum any debris.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the fan harness on both ends.

whenToCallPro: If blower replacement is required.

faq.q: What is the typical fan life?
faq.a: 8-12 years on the GB142/SSB.

title: Frost Protection Active
fullDescription:
Not strictly an error — CY is an informational code shown when the GB142/SSB has activated its built-in frost protection. The boiler runs the pump and may briefly fire to keep the heat exchanger above 5 °C.

Homeowners frequently report this in summer when an unconditioned mechanical room cools quickly overnight.
safetyWarning: Not a safety event — but ensure the boiler has gas and electricity available year-round.

fixSteps.title: Verify room temperature
fixSteps.instruction: If the boiler room is below 50 °F, add heat or insulation.

fixSteps.title: Confirm settings
fixSteps.instruction: Check that frost-protect parameters match installer guide.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot find a setting causing nuisance display.

faq.a: No — it prevents freeze damage to the boiler.

title: Boiler Water Temperature Sensor Short
shortDescription: Boiler supply temperature sensor circuit shorted.
fullDescription: Buderus 2L flags a short on the boiler water temperature sensor (commonly the supply NTC). Replacement of the sensor is the usual fix.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at PCB and measure resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Drain to sensor, swap, refill, vent.

whenToCallPro: If sensor measures good, the PCB or wiring is at fault — call a heating technician.

title: Ignition Module Communication Loss
shortDescription: Ignition module not responding to control board.
fullDescription: Code 3A appears when the boiler control board cannot communicate with the ignition module (BC-series). Often a connector or ribbon issue; sometimes the module itself fails.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing or pinched cable.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not clear 3A, the module needs replacement by a technician.

title: Return Sensor Short
fullDescription: Code 3L is a short on the return-water sensor — used by the boiler to manage condensing operation.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short after replacement requires a technician.

title: Outdoor Sensor Short
fullDescription: Buderus 4A indicates a short on the outdoor sensor input. Verify wiring and replace sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor measures good, the boiler input may be faulty — call a technician.

title: Hot Water Tank Sensor Short
fullDescription: Code 4L is a short on the indirect water heater tank sensor input, used for DHW priority heating.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Pull from tank well and swap.

whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a technician to test the boiler input.

title: Burner Lockout - Flame Loss
fullDescription: Buderus 5A latches when an established flame is lost mid-cycle. Common causes are dirty flame rod, marginal gas pressure, or vent restriction.
whenToCallPro: If cleaning and venting do not clear 5A, call a tech for combustion analysis.

title: Pressure Switch Open at Run
fullDescription: Code 5C means the air pressure switch opened during firing — venting restriction or condensate in tubing are typical causes.
whenToCallPro: If venting is clear and switch is good, call a tech.

title: Pump Run-On Fault
shortDescription: Boiler pump did not stop after demand cleared.
fullDescription: Code 6Y indicates that the circulator did not stop when commanded — usually a stuck relay on the PCB or external pump relay.
whenToCallPro: Stuck relays require board replacement; call a heating technician.

title: Gas Valve Voltage Out of Range
fullDescription: Code 7A flags abnormal voltage on the gas valve drive — a control-board fault that requires technician diagnosis.
whenToCallPro: Gas valve drive faults must be diagnosed by a licensed technician.

title: Frost Protection Active
fullDescription: Code 9A is informational, indicating frost protection is running — boiler temperature dropped below the freeze threshold and the unit fired briefly to protect itself. Not a fault unless it occurs frequently in a heated space.

fixSteps.title: Verify Ambient
fixSteps.instruction: Check that the boiler room temperature is above freezing.

fixSteps.title: Insulate as Needed
fixSteps.instruction: Insulate cold pipes near the boiler if affecting sensor.

whenToCallPro: If frost protection runs in a warm room, a sensor placement issue may exist — call a technician.

title: Calibration
fullDescription: Calibration mode required. Common boiler fault on Buderus models. Resolve following manufacturer service procedure.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — turn off gas supply and disconnect power before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor/flow
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor wiring and water flow.

whenToCallPro: Gas-appliance work usually requires Gas Safe (UK) or licensed plumber (US/CA).

faq.a: Don't use if gas leak suspected — call gas emergency.
Typically $200-1500 depending on fault.

title: Boiler Sensor Defective
fullDescription: Code DA on Buderus condensing boilers indicates the boiler supply (flow) temperature sensor is reading invalid. The control cannot manage flame modulation safely.
safetyWarning: Boiler will lock out for safety.

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open service panel and re-seat the flow sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new Buderus flow sensor.

whenToCallPro: If you are unsure, hire a Buderus-trained tech.

faq.a: Without flow temperature feedback the boiler cannot modulate.

title: Flame Loss During Operation
fullDescription: Code EA indicates the boiler lost flame signal during normal modulation. Often caused by gas pressure dips or a dirty flame rod.
safetyWarning: Boiler enters lockout. Do not bypass safety circuits.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press the reset button to clear lockout.

fixSteps.title: Clean Flame Rod
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the ionization rod.

whenToCallPro: Gas pressure issues require a pro.

faq.q: How often should the rod be cleaned?
faq.a: Annually as part of boiler service.

title: Fan Speed Out of Range
shortDescription: Combustion fan speed deviates from setpoint.
fullDescription: Code FA indicates the combustion fan RPM is outside the commanded range. Bearing wear or harness fault is typical.
whenToCallPro: Fan replacement requires combustion analyzer to verify.

faq.a: 10-15 years.

title: Gas Valve Fault
shortDescription: Gas valve drive circuit reports fault.
fullDescription: Code GA indicates the gas valve coil current is out of expected range. The valve may be failing or the wiring damaged.
safetyWarning: Gas safety system involved - call a pro.
whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.q: Can I replace the valve myself?
faq.a: No - gas work requires a licensed technician.

title: Hydraulic Sensor Fault
fullDescription: Code HA indicates the system pressure transducer is reading out of range, often due to wire damage or sensor failure.

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open panel and re-seat the pressure sensor cable.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable draining the boiler, hire a pro.

faq.a: No - pressure is a critical safety input.

title: Ignition Lockout
fullDescription: Code IA indicates the boiler made the maximum allowed ignition attempts without success and is now locked out.
safetyWarning: Do not press reset more than 3 times - excess gas accumulation risk.

fixSteps.title: Verify Gas
fixSteps.instruction: Check gas valves are open and pressure is present.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press reset once. If lockout returns, call a pro.

whenToCallPro: If two reset attempts fail, schedule service.

faq.a: Three at most - then call for service.

title: Outdoor Sensor Defective
fullDescription: Code JA indicates the outdoor reset sensor reads invalid. The boiler reverts to a fixed setpoint until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Trace and inspect the outdoor sensor cable.

whenToCallPro: Outdoor mounting may justify a pro.

faq.a: Yes, but outdoor reset is disabled - efficiency drops.

title: Condensate Trap Blocked
fullDescription: Code KA indicates the condensate level switch detected high water in the trap. The boiler will lock out to prevent flue gas spillage.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass float switches - flue gas safety hazard.

fixSteps.title: Clear Drain
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the condensate drain line and trap.

whenToCallPro: If float switch sticks, hire a pro.

faq.a: Condensing boilers extract latent heat from flue gases.

title: Heating Pump Locked
fullDescription: Code LA indicates the integrated circulator pump rotor is not turning when commanded.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before pump service.

fixSteps.title: Manual Unstick
fixSteps.instruction: Use the manual rotor screw to free the pump (if equipped).

fixSteps.title: Replace Pump
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck, replace the pump cartridge.

whenToCallPro: Cartridge replacement is a pro task.

faq.a: Often after being off through summer - sediment binds the rotor.

title: Three-Way Valve Position Fault
fullDescription: Code MA indicates the three-way valve actuator did not reach the commanded position within the allowed time.

fixSteps.title: Manual Test
fixSteps.instruction: Use the manual lever (if equipped) to verify valve movement.

fixSteps.title: Replace Actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Install new actuator or full valve.

whenToCallPro: Drain-down required - hire a pro.

faq.a: Sometimes by manually positioning the valve, but get it serviced.
